examples.en: I shower at night.
You take really long showers.
I exercise and then take a shower.
I'm tired. I want to take a quick shower and sleep.

examples.ko: 샤워는 아침에 해요? — 아니요, 저는 밤에 해요.
examples.en: Do you shower in the morning? — No, I shower at night.

explain: 샤워는 몸 전체를 씻는 거예요. 얼굴만 씻으면 ‘세수’, 욕조에서 하면 ‘목욕’이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I take a shower after exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘샤워’에 ‘-해요’를 붙여 동사처럼 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -해요 to 샤워 lets you use it like a verb.

phrases.en: I drink water after I shower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 샤워 다음에 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say what you do after a shower.

phrases.en: Where is the shower room?
phrases.nuance_ko: 헬스장이나 수영장에서 샤워하는 방이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room for showering at a gym or pool.

explain_en: A shower washes your whole body. Washing only your face is ‘세수’, and a bath in a tub is ‘목욕’.

examples.en: In the morning I just wash my face.
I'll quickly wash my face.
I wash my face and get dressed.
I wash my face with cold water.
Did you wash your face? — Yes, I just did.

explain: ‘세수’는 얼굴만 씻는 거예요. ‘세수를 씻어요’라고 하지 않고 ‘세수를 해요’라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I wake up and wash my face in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘세수를 해요’보다 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter way to say 세수를 해요.

phrases.en: I wash my face and then eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서대로 말할 때 ‘-고’로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connect with -고 to say things in order.

phrases.en: I don't wash my face on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘안’을 넣어서 하지 않는다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 안 to say you don't do it.

dict_examples.ko: 너무 바빠서 세수도 못 하고 출근하였다.
dict_examples.en: I was so busy that I went to work without even washing my face.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: ‘세수’ means washing only your face. Say ‘세수를 해요’, not ‘세수를 씻어요’.

examples.en: I went shopping with a friend on the weekend.
Shopping is my hobby.
I'm going shopping at the department store tomorrow.
Shall we have coffee together after shopping?
Online shopping is convenient.

explain: 식료품은 ‘장을 보다’라고 해요. ‘쇼핑’은 옷이나 신발처럼 구경하면서 살 때 주로 써요.

phrases.en: window shopping
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건은 사지 않고 구경만 하는 쇼핑이에요. 영어 ‘eye’에서 온 한국식 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: shopping where you only look and don't buy anything. It is a Korean-style word from English ‘eye’.

dict_examples.ko: 아이가 둘이나 있어 쇼핑이 쉽지 않아 주로 배달을 시킨다.
dict_examples.en: With two kids, shopping isn't easy, so I mostly order delivery.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: things like clothes or shoes that you browse before buying

examples.en: I go to the beach in summer.
This summer was really long.
In summer I eat a lot of watermelon.
On summer nights we eat fried chicken by the Han River.
What will you do during the summer vacation?

explain: 한국 여름은 덥고 습해요. 6월 말부터 7월까지 비가 많이 오는 ‘장마’가 있고, 아주 더운 날씨는 ‘무더위’, 밤에도 더우면 ‘열대야’라고 해요. 여름에서 가장 더운 때는 ‘한여름’이라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 저는 여름을 타서 밥을 잘 못 먹어요.
phrases.en: to be worn down by the summer heat
phrases.nuance_ko: 더위 때문에 힘이 없고 입맛이 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: feeling weak and having no appetite because of the summer heat
phrases.en_equiv: to be worn down by the summer heat

phrases.example: 여름 감기는 개도 안 걸린다는데 저는 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: even dogs don't catch summer colds (teasing someone with a summer cold)
phrases.nuance_ko: 여름에 감기에 걸린 사람을 가볍게 놀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: a light joke on someone who caught a cold in summer
phrases.en_equiv: even dogs don't catch summer colds (teasing someone with a summer cold)

explain_en: Korean summers are hot and humid. From late June into July there is a rainy season called ‘장마’; scorching weather is ‘무더위’, and nights that stay hot are ‘열대야’. The hottest part of summer is called ‘한여름’.

examples.en: That actor became a star overnight.
I've dreamed of being a star since I was little.
The stars came to the event.
My friend sings well, like a star.
I was startled to see a celebrity on the street.
A star player has joined our team.

explain: 인기가 많은 사람을 가리켜요. 하늘에 떠 있는 별에는 쓰지 않고 그때는 '별'이라고 해요. '연예인'은 직업을 말하고, '스타'는 인기가 있다는 점을 말해요.

phrases.en: I want to become a star someday too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기가 많은 사람이 되는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means becoming a popular, famous person.

phrases.en: That singer is a popular star these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스타' 앞에 '인기'를 붙이면 인기가 많다는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'ingi' (popular) makes the popularity clearer.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 좋아하던 영화 스타를 만났어요.
phrases.en: I met a movie star I liked as a kid.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영화', '운동' 같은 말을 앞에 붙여 어떤 분야의 스타인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a field like 'movie' before it to say which area the star is in.

explain_en: It refers to a popular person. It is not used for the stars in the sky, which are '별'. '연예인' describes a profession, while '스타' stresses popularity.

t90.ax: The stars came to the event.

examples.en: Every weekend I spend time out in nature.

examples.ko: 자연 보호를 위해 이 산에서는 캠핑을 못 해요.
examples.en: To protect nature, you can't camp on this mountain.
I often take nature photos.

examples.ko: 저는 도시보다 자연이 좋아서 시골로 이사했어요.
examples.en: I like nature more than the city, so I moved to the countryside.
I teach children to love nature.
I made soap with ingredients from nature.

explain: '환경'은 사람을 둘러싼 조건 전체이고, '자연'은 산, 바다, 숲처럼 사람이 만들지 않은 것을 말해요. '자연 환경', '자연 보호'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. 형용사 '자연스럽다'와 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: Protecting nature is everyone's job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연을 지키는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about protecting nature.

phrases.en: I feel good when I walk in nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산이나 숲 같은 곳에 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when being in places like mountains or forests.

phrases.en: His Korean is very natural.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자연'에서 나온 형용사로, 어색하지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective from 'jayeon', meaning not awkward.

explain_en: '환경' is the whole set of conditions around people, while '자연' means things not made by people, like mountains, seas and forests. It is often attached before other words, as in '자연 환경' and '자연 보호'. Also learn the adjective '자연스럽다' (natural).

examples.en: What kind of food do you like?
What kind of movie did you see?
What color do you like? — I like blue.
What kind of exercise do you do on weekends?
What kind of person came?

explain: ‘어떤’은 꼭 명사 앞에 와요: 어떤 색, 어떤 사람. ‘무슨 음식’은 종류나 이름을 묻고, ‘어떤 음식’은 맛이나 특징까지 물을 때가 많아요. 묻는 문장이 아닐 때는 ‘어떤 사람이 왔어요.’처럼 ‘누군가, 한’이라는 뜻도 돼요.

phrases.en: What food do you like?
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘어떤’과 비슷하지만, 종류나 이름을 물을 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 어떤, but used more for asking about type or name.

phrases.en: What kind of person do you like?
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이나 특징을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask about someone's character or traits.

phrases.en: What color do you like?
phrases.nuance_ko: ‘어떤’은 꼭 명사 앞에 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 어떤 always comes before a noun.

dict_examples.en: What kind of person is he?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: What words could she have used to persuade her father?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이런 견해에 대해 선생님 자신은 어떤 생각을 가지고 있나요?
dict_examples.en: What are your own thoughts on this view?
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 또 한 명의 여자는 고개를 숙이고 있어서 경민은 그녀가 어떤 얼굴인지 알 수가 없었다.
dict_examples.en: The other woman had her head down, so Gyeongmin couldn't tell what her face looked like.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: ‘어떤’ always comes before a noun: 어떤 색, 어떤 사람. ‘무슨 음식’ usually asks for the type or name, while ‘어떤 음식’ often asks about qualities too. In a statement like ‘어떤 사람이 왔어요.’ it means ‘some / a certain’ (Someone came).

gh: asks what or what kind; mostly in questions

p.n: Both ask the job; the replacement is more a plain 'what?', the original asks about its character.

examples.en: My phone number starts with zero-one-zero.
The first digits of a mobile number are zero-one-zero.
The locker number is zero-five.
The password is zero-one-two-three, so it's easy to remember.
The last digit of my phone number is zero.
Does the account number start with zero-two-three-four?

explain: 숫자 0은 '영'과 '공' 두 가지로 읽어요. 전화번호, 계좌번호, 비밀번호처럼 숫자를 하나씩 읽을 때는 '공'을 많이 쓰고, 점수나 영하 같은 수학·온도 이야기에서는 '영'을 써요. 둥근 물건 '공(ball)'과 소리가 같아요.

phrases.en: If a phone number starts with 010, it is a mobile number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰 번호의 앞부분을 읽을 때 숫자 0을 공이라고 한다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reading out the start of a mobile number, where the digit 0 is said as the Sino-Korean word for zero.

explain_en: The number 0 is read as either '영' or '공'. For phone numbers, account numbers and passwords, where digits are read one by one, '공' is common, while '영' is used for scores, temperatures such as 영하, and math. It sounds the same as 공 (ball).

examples.en: On my birthday my friends bought me a cake.
It always rains on my birthday.
On my birthday I had dinner with my family.
My mom's birthday is April 20th.
Since it is my birthday, I left work early today.
I wrote my friend's birthday on the calendar.

explain: 그냥 '생일'이 훨씬 흔하고, '생일날'은 생일 바로 그날을 강조할 때 써요. '생일 선물', '생일 파티'처럼 합쳐진 말에는 '생일'을 써요. 어른의 생일은 높여서 '생신'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Tomorrow is my birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훨씬 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요. 날을 강조하지 않을 때는 '생일'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The much more common word; use it when you don't stress the day itself.

phrases.en: On my birthday morning, I ate seaweed soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생일 그날의 아침을 말할 때 써요. 한국에서는 생일에 미역국을 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the morning of the birthday; in Korea people eat seaweed soup on their birthday.

phrases.en: Next week is my grandmother's birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른의 생일을 높여 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific word for an elder's birthday.

explain_en: Plain '생일' is far more common; '생일날' stresses the actual day itself. In compounds like 'birthday gift' and 'birthday party', use '생일'. An elder's birthday is honored as '생신'.

t90.ax: It always rains on my birthday.

examples.en: A famous band came to our school.
I play guitar in the school band.
I often listen to this band's songs.
My older brother started a new band with his friends.
Do you want to go see a band concert this weekend?
That band is really popular.

explain: 노래만 하는 팀은 '그룹', 악기를 직접 연주하는 팀은 '밴드'라고 구분하는 경우가 많아요. 상처에 붙이는 '밴드'(반창고)도 소리가 같아서 앞뒤 말을 보고 알아야 해요.

phrases.en: I like this group's songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이에요. 노래만 하는 팀은 '그룹', 악기를 연주하는 팀은 '밴드'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word: a team that only sings is a 그룹, one that plays instruments is a 밴드.

phrases.en: I'm going to see a band concert on Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밴드가 하는 공연을 말할 때 '밴드 + 공연'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 밴드 + 공연 for a show put on by a band.

phrases.en: I formed a band with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀을 새로 시작할 때 '만들다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 만들다 when starting a new band.

explain_en: A team that only sings is often called a '그룹', while one that plays instruments is a '밴드'. An adhesive bandage is also called '밴드' in Korean, so use the context to tell them apart.
